issue: #449 — destroy recorded no generation, so undo could not rewind past a destroy; found by the S4 pre-dogfood of the integration branch

quorum.kill_rule: any un-countered substantive objection kills the claim
refuted_claims: Record the generation BEFORE destroy touches the lock — REFUTED: inverts apply's convention (a generation records what a run PRODUCED) and rewinds to a generation identical to current.

Recording the destroy's generation under the unchanged config is enough — REFUTED by the agy lane: that generation pairs an empty lock with a config that still declares everything, and apply → destroy → apply → undo re-creates what the destroy removed. Taken: the recorded config is pruned to what survived.
The first falsifier proved the roundtrip — REFUTED: it only rewound to generation 0. Cases 4–6 now replay the destroy's own generation and the plain a → a,b → undo shape.

systems: Terraform — backs the state up and bumps the serial on EVERY state-changing command, destroy included; no config-replay undo
Nix — a profile generation for every switch; the closure and the profile always agree, so rollback is bidirectional
Puppet — no undo, only --noop; reversal is a git revert plus a run
crux.verdict: recording the destroy's generation with the config that produced it puts forjar at the Nix default (config and state agree); undo destroying what the target lacks is what makes the rollback bidirectional rather than apply-only.

agy_teamwork.verdict: review lane (plan mode, scrubbed HOME) REJECTED the first fix: the destroy generation was poisoned (empty lock under a full config) and the falsifier never replayed it. Taken.
